learning_objective: 🎯 Trace the dramatic journey of how a simple European trading company transformed into a powerful empire that ruled the Indian subcontinent for nearly 200 years!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: In the 1600s, European countries like Portugal, France, and Britain rushed to India to trade in valuable goods like cotton, silk, and spices (especially pepper and cloves). This fierce competition led to battles at sea and on land.

The British East India Company (EIC) started as a simple group of merchants. With a royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I granting them a monopoly, they set up trading posts called 'factories' along India's coasts.

The Company realized that to protect their profits, they needed political power. The famous Battle of Plassey (1757) and Battle of Buxar (1764) allowed the Company to take over Bengal, shifting them from merchants to rulers.

British policies changed everything in India. They introduced new laws, altered traditional farming to grow cash crops for Britain, and drained wealth from India to fuel the Industrial Revolution in Europe.

fun_activity.title: ⚡ The Spice Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Go to your kitchen and find 3 spices (like black pepper, cloves, or cardamom). These simple ingredients are the reason European traders first sailed all the way to India centuries ago!

quick_recap: ⭐ European nations came to India initially just to trade in highly profitable spices and textiles.
⭐ The British East India Company defeated rivals and local rulers to slowly conquer the subcontinent.
⭐ The Battle of Plassey in 1757 marked the true beginning of British political rule in India.
